pairs.subject: structured-interview-scorecards
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/interview-rubric.ts:24 Every scorecard this context computes for an experienced candidate is scored on five competencies (Technical depth, Problem-solving, Communication, Experience & fit, Motivation) with no per-level behavioural anchors, only the degree labels 'Well below bar'…'Exceptional'. That is the structure-theatre case the golden path names, so two raters (or the model) have no paragraph to settle a level on.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/interview-rubric.ts:24 Checked pipeline/jobfit/interview-rubrics.json: the experienced competencies have 0 anchors each, and the early_career ones have 5 each. The experienced model's only scale is ratingAnchors {1:'Well below bar' … 3:'Meets the bar' … 5:'Exceptional'}. The bar is named, but those are degree words, and they fail the strike-the-adjectives test. The construct lives in the rubric module this context scores against.

app/_lib/interview-scorecard.ts:212 A content hash plus rubricKeys is stamped at write time and is identical across TS and Python. Off-rubric ratings are kept and flagged (offRubric, line 42), never dropped. Legacy rows fall back to the current rubric.

app/_lib/interview-run.ts:850 Role-family coverage is stamped on the AI scorecard. interview-rubric.ts enumerates no_family / family_no_axes / family_unrecognized and discloses only no_family and family_unrecognized, so family_no_axes is silent by design. industryAxes exist for 6 families as an extension, not a fork.

app/_lib/interview-run.ts:441 Early-career entries get their own methodology, and rubricForArchetype selects a separate early_career model with rate competencies (Learning agility, Coachability…), each with its own anchors. The model is recorded only indirectly, through rubricVersion/rubricKeys; no named scoringModel field is stamped on the scorecard.

declined.subject: structured-interview-scorecards
declined.reason: None of this context's files holds a scorecard. Despite the context description, pipeline/jobfit/interview.py is a candidate-facing mock-interview question kit (STAR scaffolds tied to CV gaps), not a rubric or scorecard, and grep over the other 15 files finds no scorecard, rubric or competency construct. A not-applicable verdict would not survive the directory-wide re-search, though: the same directory, pipeline/jobfit/, holds automation.py and interview-rubrics.json, which own the scorecard but belong to other contexts. So the honest call is to decline rather than claim absence.
